version.changelog: 支持全局 AI_SKILLS_API_KEY，兼容原产品 Key；更新安装配置与请求示例，完善调用和交付规则。

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed spreadsheet-analysis connector that locally extracts spreadsheet text and sends it to a hosted analysis API when the user asks.

dimensions.detail: The local Python extractor and hosted API are proportionate to spreadsheet analysis, with documented limits of 10 MB files, 2000 non-empty rows, and 120000 extracted characters; parsed cell text and row locations are sent off-device.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation asks the user to configure an AI Skills API key in OpenClaw environment settings and restart the gateway; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users should understand it creates a reusable platform credential.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions limit use to XLSX/UTF-8 CSV extraction and named spreadsheet operations, require user authorization for sensitive data, and state that formulas, macros, and file contents are untrusted data rather than instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No service, hook, tool hijack, memory write, or background persistence was found; the only persistent element is the configured API key environment variable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is spreadsheet analysis, Q&A, comparison, evidence-backed answers, and user-requested export of prior results; the documented API operations match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending extracted spreadsheet cell text, filenames, and row locations to the AI Skills platform. Do not use it on confidential spreadsheets unless you have authorization, and protect the configured API key because it may be reused by related platform skills.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Export and asynchronous polling are documented in the skill instructions and references, limited to spreadsheet operations, and export is gated on an explicit user request for the current user's successful skill task.
[SQP-3] expected: The artifact and script messages are Chinese-only, which is a usability and audience-scope note; it does not show hidden behavior, privilege escalation, or purpose-mismatched capability.
